'''Dan Meyerstein''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] ({{langx|he|דן מאירשטיין}}; born in 1938 in Jerusalem) is an Israeli [[Academic staff|academic]] and former president of [[Ariel University]].

==Biography==
Meyerstein was born in Jerusalem in [[Mandatory Palestine]].<ref>[https://www.ariel.ac.il/wp/dan-meyerstein/wp-content/uploads/sites/175/2019/04/CV1-MS.pdf "DAN MEYERSTEIN; Curriculum Vitae"] Retrieved 22 September 2021.</ref>  He earned an M.Sc. from [[The Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] in [[Physical Chemistry]] (1961), and a Ph.D. in chemistry from the school as well (1965).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ariel.ac.il/wp/dan-meyerstein/|title=Prof. Dan Meyerstein – Personal Site|publisher=Ariel.ac.il|accessdate=22 September 2021}}</ref>

Meyerstein is Professor Emeritus of [[Ben-Gurion University of the Negev]] a member of the [[Academia Europaea]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://in.bgu.ac.il/en/Pages/news/dan_meyerstein.aspx|title=Prof. Dan Meyerstein becomes a member of the Academia Europaea|date=8 December 2011|accessdate=22 September 2021}}</ref> the [[American Chemical Society]], and the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].

In 2004, Meyerstein opened the third annual [[David Bar-Illan]] Conference on the Media.<ref>{{cite news |title=Conference looks at accuracy in reporting |work=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |date=November 2, 2004 |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P1-101973019.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517001840/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P1-101973019.html |archive-date=May 17, 2011 |via=[[HighBeam Research]] |url-access=subscription |url-status=usurped}}</ref> Concerning the [[demographic]]s of [[Israel]], Meyerstein has stated that the birthrate in the [[Judea and Samaria]] District is "crazily higher than the rest of Israel."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.jpost.com/Opinion/Op-Ed-Contributors/Demographic-threat-Nonsense|last=Rubin|first=David|title=Demographic threat? Nonsense|work=[[The Jerusalem Post]]|date=1 August 2007|accessdate=22 September 2021}}</ref>

==Views and opinions==
On academic [[boycott]]s of Israel, Meyerstein stated in ''[[The Jerusalem Post]]'' that, "I feel that many of the people involved in this boycott have little knowledge of the system here and those that do have knowledge also have the desire to abolish the state of Israel. I have always felt boycotts were a bit like burning books. This happened in [[Europe]] 70 years ago and it is part of the reason I live in Israel".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2007/jun/01/highereducation.uk1|title=Boycotts are like burning books|work=[[The Guardian]] UK|date=1 June 2007|accessdate=22 September 2021}}</ref>
